# atlassian_jira_project_role_actor (Resource)

Add a user or group to a Jira project role. One resource represents one actor (user or group) in one project role. Remove the resource to remove the actor from the role.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Add a group to the Administrators project role for a project.
# Replace project_key and role_id (from project role details) and set group_id or group_name.
resource "atlassian_jira_project_role_actor" "admin_group" {
  project_key = "PROJ"
  role_id     = "10000"
  group_name  = "jira-administrators"
  # Or: user_account_id = "abc-123" for a user, or group_id = "group-uuid"
}

output "actor_id" {
  value = atlassian_jira_project_role_actor.admin_group.id
}
```

## Import

Import by composite ID: `project_key/role_id/actor_type/value`. The resource block must exist in config before importing.

```bash
# User (value = Atlassian account ID)
terraform import atlassian_jira_project_role_actor.actor PROJ/10000/user/5b10ac8d82e05b22cc7d4ef5

# Group by name
terraform import atlassian_jira_project_role_actor.actor PROJ/10000/group/jira-administrators

# Group by ID (if value looks like a UUID)
terraform import atlassian_jira_project_role_actor.actor PROJ/10000/group/abc-123-def
```

**Import ID:** `project_key/role_id/user/<account_id>` or `project_key/role_id/group/<group_name_or_id>`. See [Importing resources](../import.md) for more.

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `project_key` (String) Project key or ID.
- `role_id` (String) Project role ID (from project role details).

### Optional

- `group_id` (String) Group ID (when adding a group). Prefer over group_name.
- `group_name` (String) Group name (when adding a group).
- `user_account_id` (String) Atlassian account ID of the user (when adding a user). Exactly one of user_account_id, group_id, or group_name must be set.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Composite ID: project_key/role_id/actor_spec (e.g. PROJ/10000/user/account-id or PROJ/10000/group/group-id).
